applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-United States Income Tax Convention, as amended (in force)
European Union-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (applies to France)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-2 et seq. (AML/CFT obligated entities), L.561-46 and R.561-1 et seq. (beneficial-owner identification and filing); Commercial Code, Articles L.233-3 and R.561-1 (control and beneficial-owner criteria); Decree No. 2024-720 of 5 July 2024 concerning access to information in the register of beneficial owners. A SARL must declare its beneficial owners to the National Register of Companies (RNE) through the electronic single window. Public access is restricted following the Court of Justice of the European Union judgment in Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20; access remains available to competent authorities and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest under applicable rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign individual shareholder's passport or national identity document and, where requested, certified French translation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport or identity-document authority in the country of issuance; translation by a qualified translator where required
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille for public documents where the Hague Apostille Convention applies; otherwise consular legalization. A passport is generally verified as an identity document rather than apostilled.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign corporate shareholder's current certificate of incorporation, registry extract, constitutional documents, and certificate of good standing or equivalent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or other competent public authority in the country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where applicable; otherwise consular legalization; provide a certified French translation when required by the filing authority, bank, or professional adviser

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign corporate shareholder's board or shareholder resolution approving the investment and appointing its representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The foreign corporate shareholder, executed by its authorized signatories; notarization where required by the governing law or recipient
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization where required, followed by Hague Apostille where applicable or consular legalization; certified French translation when required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address and, where requested, specimen signature or authority document for the proposed manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relevant utility provider, bank, public authority, notary, or other competent issuer, as applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication is document- and recipient-specific; use Hague Apostille or consular legalization only where required, and provide a certified French translation when required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: French AML-obliged banks and relevant professionals must apply risk-based customer due diligence under CMF Articles L.561-4-1 et seq., identify and assess PEPs, apply enhanced measures to foreign PEPs and high-risk cases, and report suspicions to TRACFIN where required. Screen the company, UBOs, managers, and relevant counterparties against applicable EU and French financial sanctions and UN Security Council sanctions. OFAC screening is not generally a French statutory requirement absent a US nexus, but is commonly required by US-connected banks, payment providers, and counterparties. Re-screen upon material changes and before onboarding or transactions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI); filings feed the Registre national des entreprises (RNE).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A SARL's corporate name (dénomination sociale) must be stated in its articles and filed in French corporate formalities. French accents and characters may be used. No general rule requires a foreign-language name to be transliterated into French script, but the name must be registrable and must not mislead or infringe protected rights. Check company names, trademarks, domain names, and trade names separately; registry acceptance does not establish trademark clearance.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying a regulated activity, public authority, or official status where their use is misleading or unauthorized
Banking, financial, insurance, investment-services, payment-services, and similar regulated-sector terms where use may imply authorization or require prior approval
Protected professional titles and legally protected designations unless the company is entitled to use them

Gambling, casino, lottery, betting, and gaming terminology where the proposed activity could constitute regulated gambling or create a misleading impression; obtain activity-specific French regulatory advice before use
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France has no general statutory company-name reservation period or standard 30-day name-reservation entitlement. Conduct INPI/RNE and trademark searches before filing. If a filing is rejected or a formal deficiency is notified, use the stated correction or review procedure within the deadline in the notice, provide supporting documents, and re-submit through the Guichet unique. A challenge to a formal administrative decision may be pursued through the remedy and competent court identified in that decision; a private name or trademark dispute is separate and may require negotiation or judicial proceedings.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A SARL must have a registered office in France. Domiciliation with a qualifying commercial domiciliation provider is generally permitted, subject to the provider's legal status, a written domiciliation contract, and applicable company and premises rules. A manager's residence may be used subject to statutory limits, lease, co-ownership, and planning restrictions. A virtual address alone does not establish operational substance and may be insufficient for banking, payment-provider, tax, consumer-law, or regulatory due diligence. Social-casino or virtual-slots distribution may require reassessment if the product involves stakes, prizes, or redeemable value; French gambling regulation may apply notwithstanding the proposed ISIC classification or the stated absence of a statutory license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No reliable statutory or published percentage is available. Risk is fact-specific and generally low for ordinary company registration but may increase with AML, tax, consumer-protection, payment, or gambling-regulatory concerns. Authorities may conduct inspections or request evidence of actual activity and premises; maintain access, contracts, accounting records, and operational evidence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 et seq. (SARL); Articles R.123-30 et seq. on the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés; Décret n°84-406 on the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) kept by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; all electronic filings are submitted through the INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Demande d'immatriculation au RCS (electronic corporate formation dossier, successor to the legacy M0 form).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum paid-up capital for a French SARL. Cash contributions must be fully subscribed and paid up to at least 20% at incorporation, the balance within five years; the paid-up cash must be deposited with a bank or notary in a blocked account/escrow pending RCS registration. In-kind contributions require a valuation report by a statutory auditor (commissaire aux apports) unless exempt.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the members of [FR_SARL], acting as the constitutive general meeting, hereby (i) adopt the articles of association conforming to Articles L.223-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code; (ii) subscribe in full the share capital of [amount] allocated to the members in proportion to their contributions; (iii) declare that the cash contributions have been deposited with [bank/notary] in accordance with Article L.223-7; (iv) designate the registered office at [address] and confirm the legal representation and daily management authority of [name], as gérant; (v) authorize the gérant to complete all registration filings, publish the legal notice, and procure the RCS registration. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and preparation of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Infogreffe / INPI Data (name search); no prior official name reservation is required in France
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an RCS and trademark search on the INPI/Infogreffe databases to verify availability and avoid confusion with prior registrations or proprietary rights. Prepare the statuts (articles of association) containing: proposed company name, SARL form, duration not exceeding 99 years, registered office address, precise corporate purpose (ISIC 5820 - publishing of simulated social casino and virtual slots games), capital schedule, profit-sharing rules, transfer restrictions, and management clauses.
required_dossiers: Company name search result from Infogreffe/INPI
Identity and capital allocation list of shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a third party challenges the name or the RCS data contains a conflicting name, change the proposed corporate name and adjust the draft statuts before filing; no official name opposition is issued by the registry at this pre-filing stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital subscription, payment and blocked deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A French bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations acting as depositary of the paid-up cash contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the depositary institution in the name of the company in formation. Each member pays at least 20% of the cash contributions into the account. The depositary must issue a certificate (certificat de dépôt des fonds / attestation de blocage) listing the total amount deposited and stating that the funds are blocked for the benefit of the company in formation. If the contribution is in kind, the statutory auditor's valuation report must be approved by the members.
required_dossiers: Bank or notarial certificate of blocked capital deposit
Evidence of payment from each member
Commissaire aux apports valuation report (only if in-kind contributions exist)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the depositary certificate is refused or inconsistent, request a corrected certificate or use another approved depositary; shareholders may increase or decrease the proposed capital only by a written amendment to the statuts and a corresponding re-deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the statutory incorporation notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized legal notices journal (Journal d'Annonces Légales) serving the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Insert a notice of incorporation in a JAL. Include: the proposed company name, SARL form, registered office address, corporate purpose, amount of capital, duration, names and powers of gérant(s), and the RCS registry city. Obtain the official publication certificate (attestation de parution).
required_dossiers: Attestation de parution from the JAL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice contains a material error or is published in a non-qualifying newspaper, publish a corrective legal announcement in the same or another qualified JAL and provide the new attestation, together with a cover letter, to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS incorporation filing through the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprise.fr) on behalf of the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online incorporation form on the Guichet Unique. Upload the final signed statuts and all required attachments in the prescribed order. Pay the state tax and greffe fees online. Follow the application status in the online portal and answer any clarification request from the registry within the applicable deadline.
required_dossiers: Certificat de dépôt des fonds / attestation de blocage
Acceptance of office by each gérant
Proof of occupation of the registered office (lease, electricity bill, or domiciliation contract)
Declaration of beneficial owners (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
Valid identity documents of shareholders and gérant(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry requests missing documents or information (demande de pièces complémentaires), provide them through the Guichet Unique within the notified deadline, generally 15 days. If the formality is rejected, correct and resubmit; an appeal against a refusal of registration may be made to the judge supervising the RCS (juge commis à la surveillance du registre).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration corporate identity and administrative readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INSEE / URSSAF / Service des Impôts des Entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retrieve the extrait Kbis, the official registration certificate, and the SIREN/SIRET number from INSEE. Keep the corporate records, including the share register, share transfer register, and minutes of members' decisions, at the registered office. Register as employer with URSSAF before hiring; obtain a French VAT number where relevant and open a commercial bank account using the Kbis.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis is not issued or contains errors, request correction from the Greffe; for mismatches in SIREN/SIRET or legal-form data, file a correction through the Guichet Unique. Late URSSAF registration may be cured by a late submission subject to possible administrative penalties; preserve proof of filing date.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité Nationale des Jeux (ANJ) - not competent for simulated social casino absent real-money wagering; DGCCRF for consumer fair trading; CNIL for data protection.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for free-to-play social casino publishing; no ANJ gambling licence applies because the product does not offer real-money wagering or prizes.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - software publishing under ISIC 5820 is not listed in the EIA screening categories under Article R.122-2 of the French Environmental Code.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the digital-publishing activity; no industrial wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste generation. Office electronic waste must be handled under WEEE rules and French environmental regulations on waste disposal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office must comply with fire-safety requirements of the Code du travail and, if open to the public, the Code de la construction et de l'habitation (ERP). A simple administrative office is generally not subject to a formal civil-defence permit; the employer must provide first-aid equipment, accessible emergency exits, and electrical safety checks.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministère de l'Économie et des Finances; digital portal: www.impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign shareholders form the SARL via the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); the statutory tax ID (SIREN) is issued by INSEE and the intra-community VAT number (TVA intracommunautaire) is subsequently assigned by the DGFiP. A non-established foreign entity making taxable supplies in France must submit Form 5595 (demande d'immatriculation à la TVA) to the Service des Impôts des Entreprises de l'Étranger; non-EU entities must appoint a tax representative approved by the DGFiP. Applicants must provide proof of legal existence, ultimate beneficial ownership details, and expected French turnover.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (SARL subject to Impôt sur les Sociétés — IS — at 15% reduced rate on first EUR 42,500 of taxable income and 25% standard rate; no automatic pass-through at member level)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not apply a US-style check-the-box regime. The principal elections available are: (1) option for income-tax transparency for eligible family SARLs under CGI art. 239 bis AA; (2) election to form a single VAT entity (assujetti unique) under CGI art. 256 C for closely linked French-established persons; (3) ATAD hybrid-mismatch elections or adjustments are mandatory/non-elective and are addressed via the anti-hybrid rules in the French finance acts.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 91,900 for supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for services (statutory franchise en base under CGI art. 293 B, re-assessed annually, for established small businesses). Non-established foreign persons have no registration threshold and must register for French VAT before making any taxable supply not covered by OSS/IOSS.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is introducing mandatory structured e-invoicing via the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) and accredited Partner Dematerialization Platforms (PDPs). B2B invoices must be transmitted as Factur-X, UBL or CII XML files over certified API pipelines, with B2C transaction data e-reported to the DGFiP. The implementation begins September 2026 for large and mid-size enterprises and extends to small businesses/self-employed by September 2027. There is no real-time government issuance or digital stamping; DGFiP performs continuous verification of transactional data, and platform payment data may be accessed via digital audit APIs.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of physical goods to destinations outside the EU qualify for 0% French VAT under CGI art. 262-I, provided the goods are physically transported out of France/EU under a customs export declaration and the exporter retains transport and commercial evidence. Ancillary transport, loading and freight services directly linked to the export are also zero-rated. For social-casino/digital gaming services: B2C supplies to customers outside the EU are outside the scope of French VAT (CGI art. 258); B2C supplies to EU customers are generally subject to French VAT unless simplified OSS/IOSS applies; B2B digital services are taxable at the customer's place of establishment and are normally reverse-charged.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU — Déclaration d'Exportation / Single Administrative Document)
Bill of Lading or transport document evidencing physical departure (B/L, CMR, AWB) with date and route
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer proof showing export proceeds received and repatriated to the French bank
Commercial invoice issued to the foreign buyer
Packing list and additional documents required by the customs procedure
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: In the absence of valid export proof, the DGFiP reassesses the transaction at the standard 20% VAT rate, with monthly late interest (intérêt de retard of 0.30% per month) and penalties of 40% for deliberate bad faith or 80% for organised fraud (manœuvres frauduleuses). Customs authorities may also seize and confiscate exported goods and impose a fine of up to twice the value of the goods for false export declarations. The standard reassessment window is three years, extended to ten years in cases of tax fraud; claimed input VAT credits associated with the exported goods are subject to retrospective clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), operating within the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks, together with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) as co-administrator of France's foreign financial relations regime under Articles L151-1 to L165-1 and R151-1 to R165-1 of the Code monétaire et financier (CMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both the current account and the capital account under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. France does not maintain capital controls, prior-exchange licenses, or profit-remittance authorization procedures for ordinary commercial operations. Dividend and profit remittances by a French SARL are lawful without central-bank approval, provided that: (i) a valid shareholders' distribution resolution exists; (ii) the statutory dividend withholding tax and social levies are settled (25% default rate, reduced under income tax treaties or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive); and (iii) the transfer is executed through an authorized credit institution established in the EEA and recorded in the Banque de France balance-of-payments statistics. Capital-account transactions are also unrestricted, except that inbound direct investment in sensitive sectors (defence, cybersecurity, critical infrastructure, gambling-related state monopolies) is screened under Article L151-3 CMF; software publishing and social-casino operations are outside this list and require no prior authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory surrender obligation and no mandatory conversion ratio on export proceeds; the effective conversion ratio is 0%. There is no statutory repatriation deadline: proceeds may remain in foreign-currency accounts opened with an authorized credit institution in the EEA. For statistical purposes, a resident French company must report cross-border settlements to the Banque de France when an individual transaction equals or exceeds EUR 12,500, and must retain documentary evidence of payment receipt for six years pursuant to Article L123-22 of the Code de commerce. The reserve emergency powers of the Minister of the Economy under Article L151-4 CMF could theoretically reintroduce exchange controls during a financial security crisis, but these powers are dormant and not currently exercised.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High operational feasibility, medium-to-low suitability as primary capital-escrow custodian. ACPR-licensed electronic money institutions such as Qonto, Shine, Mangopay, and Treezor offer fast remote onboarding, SEPA and SWIFT connectivity, virtual IBANs, and competitive foreign-exchange pricing. However, their EMI licences prohibit credit intermediation and their compliance policies frequently re-flag social-casino/gaming flows under sectoral reputational rules. They are optimally used for payroll, VAT, marketing, and disbursement sub-accounts rather than for shareholder capital escrow or large trade settlements requiring full balance-sheet banking relationships.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permissible under French AML rules using CNIL-compliant video-identification processes. In practice, resident French directors and managers may complete the entire KYC process remotely. Non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners of an enhanced-risk gaming-related SARL face a stricter path: the first mandate generally requires either physical attendance at a French branch of the chosen bank or a notarized and apostilled KYC dossier supplemented by a video interview with the bank's compliance officer. La Banque Postale and Crédit Mutuel frequently impose mandatory physical presence as internal policy. Appointing a French-resident manager or a delegated compliance agent (mandataire) with formal power of attorney materially accelerates account opening. The SARL must submit a current Kbis extract, the filed articles of association, a declaration of beneficial owners, and documentary evidence of the economic substance of the French operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Single-purpose French SARL controlled by non-resident beneficial owners with a newly registered corporate shell and no operational history, elevating beneficial-ownership and source-of-wealth scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a Kbis extract dated within the last three months; notarized and apostilled articles of association; a certified filing receipt from the Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE); passport copies of all directors and UBOs; proof of residential address with notarized translation for non-EU documents; parent-group organizational chart; and professional bank references from the ultimate parent's relationship bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model classified as simulated gambling / social casino, triggering bank exclusion policies designed for real-money gaming and causing false-positive labelling as gambling proceeds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit an independent French legal opinion confirming that the service is free-to-play, offers no real-money withdrawal, and therefore falls outside the ANJ (Autorité Nationale des Jeux) licensing monopoly; append PEGI age-rating certificates, Apple App Store and Google Play distribution agreements evidencing IAP-based monetization, and contractual clauses prohibiting any secondary-market conversion or resale of virtual currency into cash.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity, low-value consumer micro-transactions from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing flagged as suspicious structured activity or unexplained volume spikes in settlement files.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver Apple and Google payout reports reconciling gross consumer receipts against the 15% platform commission; platform treasury settlement confirmations (IBAN or SWIFT references); audited revenue-recognition policy; server-side transaction logs demonstrating end-user micro-payments; and a documented transaction-monitoring and user-risk-scoring framework that explains organic consumer purchasing patterns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border treasury concentration risk from U.S. and Irish platform treasury entities remitting settlement revenues into France, attracting Article L561-10 CMF anti-money-laundering declarations to TRACFIN and substance-over-form challenges.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed platform agreements (Apple Developer Program License Agreement and Google Play Distribution Agreement); intercompany treasury and service agreements; French transfer-pricing documentation; daily settlement-file samples with platform payment references; French payroll contracts, French hosting or cloud-subscription evidence, and French VAT registration records to prove genuine French economic substance and commercial rationale.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital injections and shareholder current-account advances from non-resident shareholders must be remitted through an authorized credit institution. EEA-origin payments use SEPA Credit Transfer; non-EEA payments use SWIFT MT103 with field 70 structured as 'INVS / Equity Contribution / [SARL SIREN] / [Shareholder Name]'. The receiving French bank requires the wire-transfer origin statement, the SARL's corporate authorization (board resolution for capital increase), and evidence that the funds originate from the shareholder's own account. The resident SARL must file the Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical declaration for each transaction of EUR 12,500 or more; sector-specific FDI screening is not engaged for software publishing. All inbound capital must be booked to a dedicated capital escrow account with full documentary audit trails connecting the foreign remitter, the notarial certificate, and the French corporate registry filing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EUR-denominated disbursements within the SEPA zone use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant for time-critical liquidity movements; non-EUR and non-EEA settlements use SWIFT gpi MT103 or MT202 COV with full payment-status tracking. Documentary trade transactions are supported by irrevocable confirmed letters of credit governed by UCP600 and ISBP 745, and by documentary collections under URC522 for lower-risk invoices. Intra-group treasury disbursements may be structured through centralised payment factories or cross-currency netting engines. Every outbound payment must carry the appropriate Banque de France statistical purpose code and be reconcilable against the underlying commercial invoice or intercompany agreement, with settlement logic aligned to the natural cash-conversion cycle of Apple IAP and Google Play Billing receivables. Non-EUR disbursements are matched against incoming USD settlement flows to minimize transaction exposure.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD outright forwards (plain vanilla) with maturities up to 24 months
EUR/USD FX swaps for short-term natural liquidity conversion between settlement currencies
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid emerging-market currencies, executed only with ACPR or ECB-licensed counterparties
European-style vanilla EUR/USD currency options in buyer mode only, consistent with a conservative SARL treasury mandate
Spot FX contracts for immediate conversion of platform settlement proceeds, excluding speculative leverage, crypto-derivatives, exotic structures, and uncovered option-writing positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal of RCS Registration and Confirmation of Company Data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) / RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months following the anniversary of the company's registration; actual renewal must be completed before the anniversary date in practice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal penalty of €50–150; continued non-renewal leads to formal notice and administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS, resulting in loss of legal capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Déclaration de Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (attached to annual renewal file)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, concurrently with the RCS renewal; within one month of any modification affecting beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to €15,000 and imprisonment of six months for intentional omission; blocking of the RCS renewal file until compliant.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Statutory Accounts (Dépôt des Comptes Annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court), transmitted to the tax authorities and BraBulletin Officiel des Annonces Civiles et Commerciales where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months of the end of the financial year (e.g., by 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of up to €3,000 for a legal person; compulsory strike-off warning after two consecutive failures; civil sanctions include a 2% turnover penalty imposed by court at the request of the public prosecutor.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Approval of Accounts and Corporate Decisions (Assemblée Générale Ordinaire)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal record – statutory minute book of the SARL (minutes, decision forms, and dividend approval record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the end of the financial year; must precede the deposit of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil nullity risk of shareholder resolutions if not convened within statutory deadlines; profit distribution decisions void if not approved within six months of year-end.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Liasse Fiscale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal years ending 31 December: third business day after 1 May (generally 3 May); deadline is 30 September for fiscal years ending 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late filing penalty plus late payment interest of 0.20% per month; 40% negligence penalty if the return is intentionally omitted; administrative strike-off may follow prolonged tax non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A French SARL must appoint a statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) if at the fiscal year-end it exceeds two of the following three thresholds: balance sheet total > €4,000,000; net turnover > €8,000,000; average workforce > 50 employees. Mandatory audit is also required for any SARL controlling a subsidiary or meeting group criteria, or on request of shareholders holding at least 10% of capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général – ANC Règlement 2014-03), as optionally applicable to small entities; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted only for consolidated accounts of listed companies and certain financial institutions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial owners are disclosed at incorporation. Each share transfer or change in beneficial ownership triggers a mandatory update filed with the RCS within 30 days. The annual RCS renewal implies confirmation of the last declared UBO; if any change has occurred in the preceding year, a fresh declaration must be submitted before the renewal anniversary.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des Titres Nominatifs)
Register of Securities Movements (Registre des Mouvements de Titres)
Register of Shareholders' Decisions and Minutes (Registre des Délibérations / Procès-Verbaux)

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2022)
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate 15% on first €42,500 of taxable profit for eligible SMEs (turnover < €7.6m; share capital fully paid up; ≥75% held by natural persons or eligible companies); Research tax credit (CIR) 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to €100m; Innovation tax credit (CII) 20% for prototype costs; Video game tax credit (CIJV) approx. 20% of development costs subject to statutory conditions; Young Innovative Enterprise (JEI) social tax exemptions.
stage_6.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carryforward; annual deduction capped at €1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding €1,000,000; no statutory 5-year limitation.
